children: MIG REF II INFR, LLC disclosed an 8.23% stake in Vulcan Infrastructure and Power Inc. through a new Schedule 13D. The investment closed on September 10, 2026, alongside a $10 million convertible note and a three-year warrant tied to regulatory approvals. The deal gives MIG meaningful governance rights and potential to lift its ownership once approvals arrive.

MIG secured board influence through an Investor Rights Agreement. After required approvals, MIG can nominate at least one director and place a designee on the Board’s Capital Committee, with the potential to nominate two directors if its fully diluted ownership stays at or above 7.5%. MIG also gained a non‑voting board observer seat while it holds at least 5% on a fully diluted basis.

MIG obtained a pro rata right of first offer on future equity raises and the option to earn a "Sponsor Incentive" for helping source powered land deals and tenants. The firm signaled it could buy more shares or sell holdings and may discuss strategic actions, including mergers or asset deals, as it reviews Vulcan’s plans and performance. Key terms cap MIG’s ownership at 9.99% until regulatory approvals, and the note and warrant become fully usable only after those approvals. Key quotes: "MIG will have the right to nominate one director" and "MIG will have a right of first offer to purchase... future issuances."

MIG REF II INFR, LLC is a Delaware limited liability company that directly holds the shares and is wholly owned by Machine Real Estate Fund II, LP. Machine Investment Group, LP, co-founded and led by Eric W. Rosenthal, manages the investment. Machine Investment Group focuses on opportunistic real estate credit and special situations, partnering with companies to unlock value through capital solutions and active oversight.
